editorial:
Imagine moving to the big city with big dreams only to get cheated out of every cent you own. That is exactly where you find Rie, a girl from a tiny mining town who lands in Tokyo with nothing. Just when things look their worst, she stumbles into the wild world of underground wrestling. It is a weird, loud, and totally unexpected journey that feels like a mix of a gritty sports story and a strange character study. The movie has a raw energy that makes you feel the struggle of being young and broke in a city that does not care about you.

What really makes this work is Aya Mizutorigawa, who brings a lot of heart to her role as she fights her way up. The wrestling scenes are a bit chaotic, and the pacing can feel a little jumpy, but that just adds to the messy vibe of the story. If you like oddball dramas with a lot of spirit, you will love this. You should definitely try to find a high quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture, or just look for it to rent on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: In the final act, Rie faces her biggest challenge in the ring to prove her worth. She does not necessarily become a world champion, but she finds a sense of pride and strength she never had before. The movie wraps up with her finally breaking free from the shadow of her ex-boyfriend. She realizes that the fighting was more about her own growth than winning a trophy, leaving her with a new lease on life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and weird Japanese cinema.
